law_name: Act No. 112/2016 Coll. on the Registration of Sales (EET)
description: Introduced by Babiš as Finance Minister, the act required businesses to report cash sales online to the tax administration in real time, alongside the VAT control statement introduced in the same period, to fight tax evasion. EET was suspended during the COVID-19 pandemic and abolished under the Fiala government in 2022.
significance: Babiš's best-known measure as Finance Minister and a long-running political dividing line; its reintroduction (EET 2.0) became a programme pledge of his third government.

description: Announced by Prime Minister Babiš in August 2020 and approved by the Chamber in November 2020, the tax package abolished the 'super-gross wage' as the base for personal income tax from 2021, effectively cutting income tax for employees; Finance Minister Alena Schillerová said the changes approved by the Chamber would reduce state revenue by about CZK 130 billion.
significance: The largest tax change of his first premiership, with a lasting effect on public revenue.

law_name: State coverage of renewable-energy support costs (POZE) – government resolution of 16 December 2025
description: At the first meeting of his third cabinet the government raised the state subsidy so that the budget covers the entire cost of support for renewable and supported energy sources (about CZK 17 billion a year); the Energy Regulatory Office's amended price decision removed the POZE charge from customers' bills from 1 January 2026.
significance: One of the government's first measures, lowering regulated electricity prices by about 15% for households and small businesses and more for industry, at the cost of the state budget.

law_name: Act reintroducing electronic registration of sales (EET 2.0) and related tax changes
description: Government bill reintroducing EET from 1 January 2027, extended to in-person card payments but without mandatory paper receipts, with an opt-out for the smallest flat-tax traders. The same act restores the kindergarten-fee deduction and the student tax credit and applies the 12% VAT rate to soft drinks in restaurants. Passed by the Chamber on 15 July 2026, returned by the Senate, reaffirmed on 9 September and signed by President Pavel on 17 September 2026.
significance: Delivers a flagship ANO pledge; the government expects about CZK 14 billion a year in extra revenue, which the opposition disputes.

law_name: Amendment to the Building Act (state building administration)
description: Coalition MPs' bill backed by the government that replaces municipal and regional building offices with a state building administration headed by a Territorial Development Office (Úřad rozvoje území), introduces a single merged permit procedure and treats residential projects over 10,000 m2 as public-interest 'reserved constructions'. Passed on 10 July 2026, rejected by the Senate on 20 August, re-adopted by the Chamber on 9 September and signed on 17 September 2026.
significance: The government's main housing-supply reform; critics including the Senate, mayors and environmental groups say it favours large developers and weakens municipalities, and a Constitutional Court challenge has been announced.

law_name: Act on State Employees (replacing the Civil Service Act)
description: Coalition MPs' bill supported by the government that moves ministerial civil servants from the civil-service regime to employment closer to the Labour Code, easing dismissals during reorganisations and giving ministers more say over appraisals and pay. The Chamber passed it on 26 June 2026, overrode the Senate's rejection on 8 September and, after President Pavel's veto of 17 September, overrode the veto on 14 October 2026 (104 votes).
significance: Critics, including unions, experts and the president, warn it weakens the political neutrality of the civil service; senators announced a Constitutional Court challenge in October 2026.
